guides.title: Run parameterized SQL with an owned ORM
guides.summary: Create a Node SQLite adapter, execute bound SQL through an explicit ORM instance, and close the database you own.
guides.markdown:
Use a runtime-specific entry point for the adapter. This example uses Node 22 or later and the built-in SQLite adapter, so it needs no native driver package. The neutral package root exports ORM APIs; do not import Node adapters from code that must run in Workers. For Cloudflare, use the D1 or Hyperdrive adapter from `@cossackframework/database/cloudflare` and pass the binding explicitly. Generated Cloudflare apps need Workers Node compatibility support for AsyncLocalStorage request scopes. `nodejs_als` enables only that API when the compatibility date does not already provide it. D1's binding offers atomic sequential `batch()` calls, but the ORM does not expose general interactive transactions, savepoints, connection reservation, or query cancellation; check its capability limits before relying on those operations.

When you own an ORM instance, `orm.sql` executes directly without a current request scope. Use `orm.run()` around static Active Record calls and the global `sql` tag. Close an ORM only when your code owns its adapter; request middleware owns adapters it creates.

Interpolated values become bound parameters. Use `orm.sql.id()` for table and column names. Never build identifiers from request values, and reserve `sql.unsafe()` for reviewed static SQL. Keep schema changes in migrations rather than synchronizing production schemas at startup.

The executable example uses an isolated in-memory SQLite database and proves Node package behavior only. It does not establish D1, PostgreSQL, MySQL, or Hyperdrive compatibility for SQLite-specific SQL.
